title: Algebra Basics
description: Using letters to represent unknown values and solving equations.

notes.heading: Variables and Expressions
notes.body: Letters (variables) represent unknown numbers. An algebraic expression combines numbers, variables, and operations — like 2x+3 or 5y−7. No equals sign. The number in front is the coefficient (in 4x, the coefficient is 4).

notes.heading: Solving One-Step Equations
notes.body: Use inverse operations to isolate the variable. Golden rule: whatever you do to one side, do to the other. If x+5=12, subtract 5: x=7. If 3x=18, divide by 3: x=6.

notes.heading: Expanding and Simplifying
notes.body: Expand brackets: multiply outside term by every inside term. 3(x+4)=3x+12. Simplify by collecting like terms: 5x+3+2x−1 = 7x+2. Cannot combine unlike terms like 3x and 3x².

flashcards.definition: A letter representing an unknown or changing number.
The number multiplied by a variable.
A statement showing two expressions are equal, with an equals sign.
Terms with the same variable to the same power.
flashcards.example: 3x and 5x are like; 3x and 3x² are not.

questions.explanation: Subtract 6 from both sides: 2x=8, then divide by 2: x=4.

questions.stem: Which is an expression (not an equation)?
questions.explanation: 3x−7 has no equals sign — it is an expression.
